prize_parts.citation: For a body of work that renews lyric, essay and narrative through hybrid forms in sustained, emotionally exposed dialogue with the classical inheritance.

statement.case_for: My opening first place for Anne Carson holds after reading colleagues' arguments. On voice, her work is recognisable within a few lines, with its cool syntax, abrupt turns and mix of scholarly exactness and exposed feeling. On form, Autobiography of Red (a verse novel built on the Geryon material) and Nox (an elegy for her brother that combines translation, philological commentary and archival fragments in one object) do more than mix genres. In both, the formal decisions carry the meaning, so the hybrid structure is the argument and not decoration. Intellectual depth shows in how consistently the work returns to loss, desire, translation and the limits of language, from the essays on Eros and on Greek literature to the later verse and the stagings of Greek drama. Sustained quality is plausible across several decades, though I have not independently verified the full corpus. I treat the shared first-place ranking in the openings as no argument for merit. The case rests on the writing, and I have tried to test it against the strongest objections below.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the achievement is partly bound to page design, typography and allusion to Greek texts, which are hard to judge in translation and from public knowledge alone. A second concern is whether the committee can separate the original literary achievement from the scholarship and translation that surround it. Related to this is whether much of the work is fragmentary or short in scale, which bears on the 'sustained' criterion. If the committee reads her mainly as a scholar-poet whose force depends on a specialist inheritance, the claim to breadth of significance becomes weaker, though I do not think that is the better reading.

responses.point: Sward ranked Carson first but warned that her heavy allusiveness to Greek texts means her weight as literary achievement, as distinct from scholarship, needs close reading. She placed Zurita second and Can Xue third.
responses.response: I take the allusiveness concern seriously and think it is the right test. My answer is that in Autobiography of Red and Nox the classical material is not a prerequisite for the emotion. The Geryon story works as a modern love narrative for a reader who has never met Stesichorus, and Nox works as a grief object whatever one knows of Catullus. The scholarship extends the work without being required to enter it. I would still place the translations and academic writing in the context of the citation and not make them carry it. I disagree with your ordering of Zurita and Can Xue above Cărtărescu. Can Xue's method is radical, but the question of whether its sameness limits development across the corpus is, for me, less settled than the case for Cărtărescu's late expansion.

responses.point: Olsson argued that Carson's formal invention and intellectual depth are sustained over decades, that the citation should rest on formal renewal of poetry and the essay, and that the scope should not be reduced to her translations or academic work. He also noted that his assessment relies on general public knowledge and not on a reading of the full corpus.
responses.response: I agree on scope, and I would make it a condition of the citation that it names the hybrid practice, with the original writing as its core. I share your caution about corpus knowledge. Our agreement here is not independent verification of her later output, which remains an open question for me. Where I would qualify your framing is the phrase about a 'timing that is appropriate'. That should not enter the literary case, and I have not relied on it. My argument rests on the formal achievement and on its durability across the whole body of work.

responses.point: Palm praised Carson's inventive handling of form and her combination of classical learning with emotional exposure, but noted that the oeuvre is often short or fragmentary in scale, so the main weighing is its sustained development into later work.
responses.response: This is the most important qualification on maturity, and I think it cuts both ways. The brevity and fragmentary quality are part of the method, since compression, interruption and the open fragment are central to her handling of grief and translation. Even so, the committee should ask whether the later books deepen the project and not just repeat the gesture. I cannot settle that from my knowledge of the later work, so I list it as an uncertainty and not as a settled strength. I would use Zurita as the comparison. His oeuvre is plainly larger in scale, but its strong rootedness in a single historical context raises its own question about how it travels beyond that context.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg called Carson's formal invention exceptional and her influence durable, but flagged that experimental or ephemeral items such as boxed or performance pieces may be less representative of the core achievement, and that his knowledge of her most recent decade is thin.
responses.response: I agree that the object-like and performance pieces should not define the case, and Nox is the one exception I would defend, because its design is inseparable from the elegy. I share the gap in knowledge about the recent decade. That gap argues for modesty in the citation wording and not for lowering her rank, but I accept that it is a real uncertainty and not something I can resolve here. I also note that you ranked Yan Lianke above Zurita and Can Xue. I rank him lower for now because I cannot judge the Chinese prose and the English versions vary in quality, and I would not want his political context to enter the merit assessment.

uncertainties: Whether Carson's later work (the most recent decade) deepens the project or repeats it is not something I can verify from public knowledge.
How the committee should weigh her translations from Greek and her classical scholarship against her original writing remains a judgment call.
Much of the effect of Nox and similar works depends on physical design and typography, which cannot be fully assessed in a text-only or translated reading.
I have not independently verified any text. Translation coverage of her work into Swedish and other languages is unknown to me.
Whether the compressed, fragmentary scale of much of the work satisfies the criterion of sustained significance across the oeuvre is contested.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My background in literary non-fiction and my biographical work on Nobel and Wallenberg are context only. No shortlisted writer appears among my listed connections. My simulated vote is a modeling assumption, since the supplied sources do not say whether a co-opted member votes in committee.
